text:
tessa: Heads-up — we've been seeing a regression in 99th pct latency for AWQ weight-only (GS=32) on p4d under steady 70–90 req/s. baseline looked fine, but the last two runs spiked to ~240ms (was ~120ms).

mike: repro steps? which model and config?

tessa: repro is simple: run rrt-bench against model `redwood/opt-6.7b-awq-int8-wonly` with batch=1, pipe=async, kv_cache enabled. Observed with default packer=serial, prefetch=on.

cheng: have you captured perf counters / sampler traces? sounds like KV churn or pack/unpack blocking the kv-hotpath.

ciara: I pulled a short perf trace during a spike. pasted below — it's noisy but shows lots of `kv_cache.eviction` churn and repeated `unpack_weights` on the hot path.

ciara: ```
# run: ./bench --model awq-wonly --batch 1 --reqs 80 --trace sampler.log
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] req=1234 start
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] packer: group_size=32 stride=64 -> pack_latency=0.45ms
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.78, evict=14/s, spill=3/s
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] kernel: chosen=int8-awq-gs32-kernel-v2, latency=1.8ms
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] unpack_weights: 1.2ms (hot)
[2026-03-10T12:03:02Z] req=1234 finish total=245ms (tail)
```

tessa: note the repeated `unpack_weights` entries right before tail latency — suggests we're reloading weight blocks into fast buffers per request. maybe pack alignment or slab allocation causing de-dupe miss.

mike: interesting. if packer stride misaligns with allocator slab size, you get partial fills and extra memcpy / unpack operations. can you try gs=16 and gs=64 to see slope?

ciara: did quick sweep: gs=16 99p ~130ms, gs=32 99p ~240ms (spike), gs=64 99p ~140ms. so non-monotonic at 32.

cheng: that smells like an eviction working set boundary right at gs=32. how big is the kv-cache slab / page size? default slab=256KB currently. group block bytes with awq-int8: approx 8KB per group (including headers) -> 32 groups ~256KB boundary.

tessa: exactly. if group packing * group_size hits slab boundary, we get an extra slab lookup and evictions. propose two short fixes: (1) bump slab size to 512KB for awq weight-only models, or (2) adjust packer to avoid packing group boundary exactly on slab edge (pad or prefer different stride).

mike: both are viable. bumping slab reduces eviction but increases mem pressure and may affect other models. packer padding seems safer and cheaper. could also do adaptive packer that probes group_size alignment at startup.

ciara: I implemented a quick patch to pad packers by 4KB when group footprint % slab_size == 0. Ran benchmark: 99p dropped from 240ms -> 128ms, average unchanged.

perf-bot: perf-test: 2206789456-2026-03-10T12:45:00Z completed. baseline: 99p=240ms, patched: 99p=128ms, p95 delta -12ms. artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/2206789456/trace.tar.gz

cheng: nice. we should add a kernel-choice guard too: if packer introduces padding, prefer kernel variant with lower unpack cost (v1 vs v2). some kernels pay more for unaligned weights.

mike: also add an opt-in config in model catalog: `packing.alignment_guard: true/false` and `packing.pad_bytes: 4096`. default true for awq-wonly models. add telemetry metric `packing.pad_applied` and `kv_eviction_rate`.

tessa: deploying patch to staging. will run longer 6h soak and report. thanks for quick turn. :tada:

mike: followup items: (1) perf-team to quantify mem-pressure impact if we bump slab, (2) packer team to add alignment guard + unit tests, (3) runtime to expose telemetry and ensure SLO alerts for packing.pad_applied > 5% of requests.

ciara: I'll open PR with the quick patch and bench artifacts. link incoming.

tessa: PR looks good. after soak, let's ship to prod with feature-flag and monitor `kv_cache.eviction` and 99p latency.

mike: optional later: explore static calibration tune for AWQ that prefers group sizes avoiding slab boundaries during quantization phase. could bake into quantizer recommendations.

tessa: agreed. closing for now. ping me if you see regressions in other models after padding change. :eyes:
